Fix odd-value forcing in kmap construction and neighbor search — kmap/neighbor search used raw centroid values (signed/unsigned bug), fix used signed arithmetic and odd-forced centroid values to match inference-time decoding. REGRESSION: odd-forcing reduced neighbor list diversity by conflating centroids with different raw values that decode to identical odd values.

Scale-aware robust post-d grid index refinement (≥2/3 scale acceptance) + closed-form optimal d recomputation — REGRESSION: robust criterion rejected too many valid index changes, reducing post-d refinement benefit; closed-form d shift further compounded mismatch.

Odd-forced centroid scoring in neighbor search only (not kmap) — REGRESSION: odd-forced scoring changed neighbor selection priority, producing same KL (0.712151) as exp-057 which made a similar change. Even-valued centroids are rare in learned grids, so the scoring change has minimal effect but slightly reduces codebook diversity perception.

Post-refinement per-sub-block level recomputation using LS-optimal scale from updated indices — CATASTROPHIC REGRESSION: recomputing levels after index refinement breaks the index-scale coupling. Even ±1 level changes shift the quantized scale enough to invalidate post-d grid indices, causing reconstruction error to soar. Same failure mode as exp-050/ex-054 (KL~1.2).
Finer d optimization grid (17 candidates at 2% step instead of 9 at 4%) — IMPROVEMENT: finer granularity finds better d values that 4% step misses. KL improves from 0.710657 to 0.704868 (-0.81%).

Wider d optimization range (±24% at 2% step, 25 candidates) — REGRESSION: wider range includes suboptimal d candidates near the edges. Some superblocks select d from the extended range that produces worse level quantization for the current grid indices, increasing reconstruction error. The ±16% range from exp-061 is optimal.
Finer d optimization grid (33 candidates at 1% step, same ±16% range) — IMPROVEMENT: finer 1% step finds better d than 2%. KL improves from 0.704868 to 0.702666 (-0.31%).

Finest d optimization grid (65 candidates at 0.5% step, ±16% range) — IMPROVEMENT: 0.5% step finds better d values that coarser steps miss. KL improves from 0.702666 to 0.699009 (-0.52%). Unexpectedly large gain suggests structured error landscape below 1% resolution.

Ultra-fine d optimization grid (129 candidates at 0.25% step, ±16% range) — REGRESSION: despite being a superset of the 0.5% grid, the 0.25% step produces slightly worse KL (0.70363 vs 0.69901). Likely floating-point error accumulation differences across 129 iterations in the d optimization loop affecting tiebreaking. The 0.5% step represents the optimal resolution for the d search.

Post-d refinement with centroid-aware sign parity re-evaluation — CATASTROPHIC REGRESSION: sign re-evaluation after index change doesn't properly account for derived parity of element 8 (parity bit). The error computation for sign flip candidates ignores element 8's derived sign, causing selection of apparently-optimal sign patterns that are actually worse when parity is included. Fundamental bug in error computation.

Narrower d optimization range (±8% at 0.5% step, 33 candidates) — REGRESSION: ±8% range misses the true optimal d for some superblocks where the best d is beyond 8% of d_base. Exp-064's ±16% at 0.5% step (65 candidates) is the optimal configuration.

Quantizer-aware K-means assignment (scale-aware dot-product instead of L1) — CATASTROPHIC: scale-aware assignment groups samples by direction, but component-wise centroid update destroys shape information, causing degenerate feedback loop. Same failure mode as exp-037 (KL=12.3 collapse).

kmap2 second-best centroid evaluation (L2 second-closest tried as alternative during quantization) — REGRESSION: second-best centroid adds noise, L2-first is already optimal for weighted-L1 quantizer objective

Importance-weighted 2-bit level assignment during quantization (alpha=0.3) — REGRESSION: weighting biased centroid selection toward off-map patterns, increasing neighbor search dependence and reducing quality

Exhaustive 4-bit level search (replace nearest-int with weighted-reconstruction-error minimization) — CATASTROPHIC REGRESSION: selecting levels different from nearest-int breaks the index-scale coupling. The d optimization assumes nearest-int levels (step 2); when the final level selection (step 3) diverges, the d is suboptimal for the chosen levels. The post-d refinement (step 4) can only partially compensate by changing grid indices for the wrong scale_q. Same failure mode as exp-050/054/056/060.

Quantization-Aware Centroid Refinement (QAT) — blend K-means centroids with scale-aware targets using LS-optimal scale per assigned sample. After K-means+snap, recompute assignments, compute target values that give zero error at LS-optimal scale for each training sample, average per centroid, blend with K-means (alpha=0.5). REGRESSION: scale-aware targets were nearly identical to K-means centroids for well-clustered data, tiny per-dim perturbation added noise not signal.

Joint d+level optimization in a single pass — exhaustive level search over 0..15 during d optimization and final encoding. CATASTROPHIC REGRESSION: per-sub-block independent level optimization during d evaluation destroys the joint superblock scale balance. Same failure mode as exp-050/056/060. Quantize time exceeded 5-min limit (490s).
